triage.summary:
Closed at Θ(√(KT)), on one reading of the setting. The bounds in the database don't use the best available results. The setting lists no corruption level C (parameters is empty), so I treated the problem as worst case over C. If C is unbounded, the minimum gap Δ stops restricting the adversary. Any environment satisfies Reg ≥ Σ Δ_i E[N_i] − C once C ≥ ΔT, whatever Δ is.

- **Upper bound:** Tsallis-INF (Zimmert & Seldin, JMLR 2021, arXiv 1807.07623) gets O(√(KT)) in the adversarial regime, with no log K factor. It also gets O(Σ log T/Δ_i) in the self-bounding regime. Audibert & Bubeck's INF/MOSS family also removes the √log K factor. This is from what I know already, not from a source I opened this session.
- **Lower bound:** Auer, Cesa-Bianchi, Freund & Schapire (SIAM J. Comput. 2002) prove a matching Ω(√(KT)) minimax bound. Their hard instance is stochastic, so it lies inside the adversarial self-bounding class. The database's lower bound min(K/Δ, ΔT) already reaches √(KT) when Δ = √(K/T). When C is unbounded, the Auer et al. instance still applies at any Δ.

So the √log K in the database's upper bound is extra, and the stored per-variable exponents for Δ and T are not tight in this worst-case-over-C reading.

**Caveat:** if C is meant to be a fixed parameter, the right comparison changes. That rate is O(K log T/Δ + √(C·K log T/Δ)) from Masoudian & Seldin, COLT 2021 (arXiv 2103.12487). With C = 0 it is matched by the Ω(K log T/Δ) stochastic lower bound. Whether the √C term is tight was not checked here.

**Sources checked:** I saw search results for Tsallis-INF and its improved analysis, and for the 2002 paper's matching lower bound. I did not open any of the full texts, so the proofs and exact constants are unchecked.

papers.title: Tsallis-INF: An Optimal Algorithm for Stochastic and Adversarial Bandits
papers.claim: Defines the adversarial regime with a self-bounding constraint. Gets logarithmic regret in that regime while keeping adversarial-optimal O(√(KT)) worst-case regret.

papers.title: The Nonstochastic Multiarmed Bandit Problem
papers.claim: Gives a matching lower bound of order √(KT) for adversarial K-armed bandits. The hard instance is stochastic, so it falls inside the self-bounding class.

papers.title: Improved Analysis of the Tsallis-INF Algorithm in Stochastically Constrained Adversarial Bandits and Stochastic Bandits with Adversarial Corruptions
papers.claim: Under a (Δ, C, T) self-bounding constraint, gives a regret bound with a logarithmic term plus a √C-type term. This is the relevant rate if C is a fixed parameter.

triage.summary:
The gap is closed in the worst-case regime: the minimax regret is Θ(√(KT)).

**Why the lower bound applies.** The adversarial regime with a self-bounding constraint includes the fully adversarial case: take the corruption level C_sb to be of order T. So any adversarial lower bound for decoupled bandits carries over, and the database's lower bound, √(T log K), is too weak.

**Where the √(KT) lower bound comes from.** Avner, Shamir & Mannor (ICML 2012, arXiv 1205.2874) state it, but not as a fully proved general theorem. Footnote 1 in their Section 3 says the standard Ω(√(kT)) bandit lower-bound construction "can be shown to apply to a 'decoupled' algorithm as well". There is no numbered theorem or proof for this. Their Theorem 6 does prove a c√(kT) bound, but only for algorithms with a fixed querying distribution. The argument is plausible because the learner still observes only one arm per round.

**Later papers that treat this as settled.** Both describe the bound as Ω(√(KT)) and call √(KT) minimax optimal:
- Rouyer & Seldin (COLT 2020) give Decoupled-Tsallis-INF, with O(√(KT)) adversarial regret.
- Kim, Lee & Oh (NeurIPS 2025, arXiv 2510.12152) say Avner et al. "established a lower bound of Ω(√KT), matching that of the standard MAB", and give a minimax-optimal O(√(KT)) FTPL policy. They cite the bound rather than proving it.

**Matching upper bound.** O(√(KT)) is achieved, consistent with the database's jin2023improved bound.

**What the verdict covers.** Only the worst-case exponents: T^{1/2} and K^{1/2}. The finer instance-dependent bound in terms of Δ and C_sb for decoupled feedback was not checked. Kim, Lee & Oh only analyse the stochastically constrained adversarial regime, not the self-bounding regime with corruption.

papers.title: Decoupling Exploration and Exploitation in Multi-Armed Bandits (Avner, Mannor, Shamir)
papers.claim: Footnote 1, with no numbered theorem or proof: the standard Omega(sqrt(kT)) bandit lower-bound construction also applies to decoupled algorithms. Theorem 6 proves c*sqrt(kT) only for algorithms with a fixed querying distribution.

papers.title: Tsallis-INF for Decoupled Exploration and Exploitation in Multi-armed Bandits (Rouyer, Seldin)
papers.claim: Decoupled-Tsallis-INF achieves the minimax-optimal O(sqrt(KT)) regret in the adversarial regime and time-independent regret in the stochastic regime.

papers.title: Follow-the-Perturbed-Leader for Decoupled Bandits: Best-of-Both-Worlds and Practicality (Kim, Lee, Oh)
papers.claim: Cites Avner et al. (2012) as having established an Omega(sqrt(KT)) adversarial lower bound for decoupled bandits. Its FTPL policy attains O(sqrt(KT)) and is called minimax optimal.

triage.summary:
The gap is already closed, and by the same paper the database cites for its lower bound: ito2021optimal. The upper bounds in the database carry over from bandit algorithms (Tsallis-INF; Masoudian & Seldin), so they scale as sqrt(KT) and K log T. Those are too loose for full-information feedback.

Shinji Ito, "On Optimal Robustness to Adversarial Corruption in Online Decision Problems" (NeurIPS 2021, arXiv 2109.10963), has a matching upper bound for the expert problem. Its Theorem 3 covers Hedge with the decreasing learning rate η_t = sqrt(8 log N / t). In the adversarial regime with a self-bounding constraint, it shows pseudo-regret ≤ 33 + 100 log N/Δ + 10 sqrt(C log N/Δ). Hedge also has the standard worst-case bound sqrt(2T log N) + log N/8. The paper combines the two into O(min{log N/Δ + sqrt(C log N/Δ), sqrt(T log N)}). Here N is the number of experts, i.e. K.

The paper's Theorem 5 lower bound has exactly the same form, and the paper says it is tight up to a constant factor. So the order is known in every variable:
- K: log K, not sqrt(K).
- T: sqrt(T log K) in the worst case.
- Δ and C: log K/Δ + sqrt(C log K/Δ).

The database's upper-bound entries should be replaced by Ito's Theorem 3 plus the standard Hedge bound. Note that the worst-case sqrt(T log N) term is not stated in Theorem 3 itself. It comes from combining Theorem 3 with Theorem 1 (the standard Hedge bound); I read this in the ar5iv full text. Also relevant is earlier work by Amir et al. (2020), which showed decreasing Hedge has a linear dependence on C; I saw this only in a search-result summary of Ito's related work, not the paper itself.

papers.title: On Optimal Robustness to Adversarial Corruption in Online Decision Problems (Shinji Ito, NeurIPS 2021)
papers.claim: Expert problem, adversarial regime with a self-bounding constraint. Theorem 3: decreasing-rate Hedge has pseudo-regret ≤ 33 + 100 log N/Δ + 10 sqrt(C log N/Δ). Combined with the standard Hedge bound sqrt(2T log N), this gives O(min{log N/Δ + sqrt(C log N/Δ), sqrt(T log N)}). Theorem 5 gives a matching lower bound, tight up to a constant factor.

triage.summary: The worst-case log gap in T looks closed for bounded rewards. Tsallis-INF (Zimmert & Seldin) has O(sqrt(KT)) adversarial regret (seen in a poster summary, not the theorem itself) and explicitly covers corrupted stochastic bandits as a special case. My own inference, not stated in the papers: running it on the corrupted losses and paying at most 2C to switch to the uncorrupted reference gives O(sqrt(KT) + C) worst-case regret. That matches the Omega(sqrt(KT)) lower bound (and the trivial Omega(C)) with no log T factor. Caveat: Tsallis-INF assumes losses in [0,1]. For unbounded Gaussian rewards I found no paper stating a log-free sqrt(KT)+C bound, and shifting or truncating the losses likely brings back a sqrt(log T) factor. So the gap is resolved for bounded rewards and only a technicality remains under the strict Gaussian model.

papers.title: Tsallis-INF: An Optimal Algorithm for Stochastic and Adversarial Bandits (Zimmert, Seldin)
papers.claim: O(sqrt(KT)) adversarial regret (constant not checked) while also covering stochastic bandits with corruptions (Lykouris et al.) without knowing the regime. Inference, not in the paper: adding at most 2C to switch to the uncorrupted reference gives O(sqrt(KT)+C) worst-case corrupted regret for losses in [0,1].

papers.title: Improved Analysis of the Tsallis-INF Algorithm in Stochastically Constrained Adversarial Bandits and Stochastic Bandits with Adversarial Corruptions (Masoudian, Seldin)
papers.claim: Improved corrupted-regime bound: a log T term plus sqrt(C * sum 1/Delta_i * log T).

papers.title: Better Algorithms for Stochastic Bandits with Adversarial Corruptions (Gupta, Koren, Talwar)
papers.claim: BARBAR achieves O(KC) + O~(sum 1/Delta_i) regret.

triage.summary: The upper bound comes from Theorem 5 of Bai, Jin, Wang, Xiong (NeurIPS 2021, arXiv:2102.11494). That theorem is about linear bandit Stackelberg games and gives Õ(d²/ε²) queries, so the "K" in this entry is really the feature dimension d. Appendix E.2 of the same paper proves an Ω(d/ε²) lower bound and says the upper bound "has at most an O~(d) factor from the lower bound". It does not call this an open problem in the part I read; the conclusion was not checked. For finite-action bandit games the paper's bounds already match: Theorem 2 gives Õ(AB/ε²) and Theorem 3 gives Ω(AB/ε²). Searches for follow-up work improving the linear case to d/ε² found nothing (citing papers were not checked systematically). Two related papers turned up: arXiv:2301.11518 studies a different model (omniscient follower, regret objective), and arXiv:2405.06977 appeared only as a search hit and was not read. "li2023tight" was not found or checked. The gap is neither closed nor explicitly stated to be open.

papers.title: Sample-Efficient Learning of Stackelberg Equilibria in General-Sum Games
papers.claim: Theorem 5: Õ(d^2/eps^2) queries for linear bandit games; Appendix E.2: Ω(d/eps^2) lower bound, at most Õ(d) factor gap. Bandit games (finite A,B): tight Θ~(AB/eps^2) (Thms 2,3).

papers.title: Online Learning in Stackelberg Games with an Omniscient Follower
papers.claim: Different model: says worst-case sample complexity for ε-Stackelberg regret is at least exponential even with linear structure; does not address the d vs d^2 gap.

triage.summary: The gap is neither confirmed closed nor confirmed open. The lower bound can be raised: a constant (uninformative) context reduces the setting to the two-armed Bernoulli bandit. Kulkarni & Lugosi ("Minimax Lower Bounds for the Two-Armed Bandit Problem", c.1997) show minimax regret of order √T, and arXiv 2202.05767 gives constants 0.612 ≤ liminf M(T)/√T for the general two-armed Bernoulli bandit, attributed to earlier work. Both were seen in search snippets only, not fetched. This improves the database's √T/log T lower bound to Ω(√T). The upper bound stays at √T·log^{3/4}T (jin2026nearly), which I could not find, so a log^{3/4}T gap remains. I found no matching O(√T) upper bound and no statement that the residual gap is open. The setting's lack of a function class makes the upper-bound question ill-specified.

papers.title: Minimax Lower Bounds for the Two-Armed Bandit Problem (Kulkarni, Lugosi)
papers.claim: Minimax regret of the two-armed bandit is of order sqrt(n) under mild conditions; applies to K=2 Bernoulli with trivial context, giving Omega(sqrt(T)).

papers.title: A PDE-Based Analysis of the Symmetric Two-Armed Bernoulli Bandit
papers.claim: Cites known bounds 0.612 <= liminf M(T)/sqrt(T) <= limsup M(T)/sqrt(T) <= 0.752 for the general two-armed Bernoulli bandit.

triage.summary: Neither closed nor confirmed open. Two searches found no 2026 paper by Jin matching "jin2026nearly". The setting has an empty function class, so the comparator (all policies, a finite policy class or a linear class) is unclear and I couldn't check the upper bound. From background knowledge, not verified this session: if the comparator includes the best fixed arm, the standard Ω(√T) lower bound for 2-armed bandits applies (a single context reduces the problem to an ordinary bandit). That beats √T/log T and would leave a log^{3/4} T gap. The closest result found: per the search summary, Kim, Yang and Jun (arXiv:2211.05632) prove O(d√(T log T)) for linear contextual bandits with stochastic contexts and say it is unknown whether a matching Ω(d√(T log T)) lower bound holds. That suggests the log factor is open in that related linear setting; I did not open the paper. Nothing found closes this exact gap.

papers.title: Contexts can be Cheap: Solving Stochastic Contextual Bandits with Linear Bandit Algorithms
papers.claim: O(d√(T log T)) regret for contextual linear bandits with stochastic contexts. Per the search summary, the paper says it is unknown whether a matching Ω(d√(T log T)) lower bound holds with stochastic contexts. The paper itself was not opened.

papers.title: Optimal Regret for Policy Optimization in Contextual Bandits
papers.claim: Levy & Mansour: Õ(√(T·|A|·log|F|)) high-probability regret for policy optimization in stochastic contextual bandits with a function class F (a related but different setting).

triage.summary:
For fixed, undirected, strongly observable feedback graphs, two published results together give a worst-case regret of Θ(√(αT(1+ln(K/α)))) for each pair (K, α). This closes the gap between the database's bounds (upper √(KT) and √(T log T); lower √(αT)). Two things are left open: directed graphs, and a proof written out specifically for Gaussian noise.

**Upper bound.** Eldowa, Esposito, Cesari and Cesa-Bianchi (NeurIPS 2023, arXiv:2305.15383) prove O(√(αT(1+ln(K/α)))). They use FTRL with q-Tsallis entropy and tune q to α. The bound holds against an adaptive adversary, so it also holds for stochastic i.i.d. losses. It is proved for undirected graphs, with or without self-loops, including time-varying sequences. Their own lower bound, Ω(√(αT ln K / ln α)), uses a graph drawn at random each round, so it does not cover the fixed-graph case on its own.

**Matching lower bound.** Chen, He and Zhang (ICML 2024, arXiv:2307.07264) prove Θ(√(T Σ_k log(m_k+1))) for "m-MAB". This is a fixed feedback graph made of disjoint cliques of sizes m_k, which is undirected and strongly observable. The lower bound uses stochastic Bernoulli arms and a reduction to best-arm identification. Take α cliques, each of size K/α. The bound becomes Ω(√(αT log(K/α+1))), which matches the Eldowa et al. upper bound. Eldowa et al. state this themselves: Chen et al.'s fixed disjoint-clique lower bound "would imply" their algorithm is worst-case optimal up to constants for every pair (K, α).

**Consequences for the database:**
- The lower bound √(αT) is loose by a factor of √(log(K/α)) when α < K.
- The upper bound √(KT) is loose when α ≪ K.
- When α = K, both results reduce to the standard bandit rate Θ(√(KT)).

**Caveats:**
1. Both results are for bounded or Bernoulli losses. The Gaussian, known-σ version follows by the usual arguments, but I did not see it stated explicitly.
2. For directed strongly observable graphs, Eldowa et al. say extending the result is "considerably harder" and leave it open. The best directed bound they cite is O(√(αT(ln K)³)). So if this database entry covers directed graphs, the log gap there is still open.

papers.title: On the Minimax Regret for Online Learning with Feedback Graphs (Eldowa, Esposito, Cesari, Cesa-Bianchi)
papers.claim: Upper bound O(sqrt(alpha T (1+ln(K/alpha)))) via FTRL with q-Tsallis entropy for undirected strongly observable graphs. Lower bound Omega(sqrt(alpha T ln K / ln alpha)) using Bernoulli losses and a graph drawn at random each round. Notes that Chen et al.'s fixed disjoint-clique lower bound implies worst-case optimality up to constants for every (K, alpha). Directed graphs are left open as considerably harder.

papers.title: On Interpolating Experts and Multi-Armed Bandits (Chen, He, Zhang)
papers.claim: Minimax regret Theta(sqrt(T sum_k log(m_k+1))) for m-MAB, i.e. a fixed feedback graph of disjoint cliques. The lower bound uses Bernoulli arms via best-arm identification and extends to graph feedback in terms of clique cover parameters. With alpha equal cliques it gives Omega(sqrt(alpha T log(K/alpha+1))), matching the Eldowa et al. upper bound.

triage.summary: The polynomial gap in K (upper K^{3/4} vs lower K^{1/2}) is closed up to log factors. The database's upper bound looks like Jin's linear-bandit result (arXiv:2609.15170) applied with d=K, which is loose for the K-armed case. K arms with stochastic rewards and changing action sets is the stochastic sleeping-bandit problem, with regret measured against the best available arm (equivalently the best ordering). UCB on the available arms gets O(sqrt(KT log T)) by the standard confidence-width sum, even when availability is adversarial, so it covers stochastic availability too (this argument is my own reasoning). A search snippet credits Kleinberg et al. (COLT 2008 / MLJ 2010) with an Õ(sqrt(TK log T)) bound for stochastic rewards, but I could not open that paper (certificate error / 403). I did read Huang, Hu & Pan (arXiv:2605.09277, INFOCOM 2026): under adversarially varying availability, CL-SG gets regret <= C ln T sqrt(mNT) + 2 sqrt(6 mNT ln T), and they cite earlier sqrt(mNT ln T) UCB bounds for stochastic and adversarial availability. With m=1 this gives O(sqrt(KT) log T). Caveats: their lower-bound construction needs N >= 400m, and I did not confirm their reward assumptions (bounded vs subgaussian). The lower bound Omega(sqrt(KT)) already holds when every arm is always available (wu2015online). So the minimax rate is Theta~(sqrt(KT)), and only a log T factor remains open.

papers.title: Worst-Case Regret Bounds for Combinatorial Thompson Sampling in Sleeping Semi-Bandits (Huang, Hu, Pan)
papers.claim: CL-SG gets O~(sqrt(mNT)) worst-case regret (explicitly <= C ln T sqrt(mNT) + 2 sqrt(6mNT ln T)) in sleeping semi-bandits with adversarially varying availability, with a matching lower bound; cites earlier O(sqrt(mNT ln T)) UCB bounds under stochastic and adversarial availability. With m=1 this gives O(sqrt(KT) log T) for K-armed sleeping bandits. Reward assumptions not confirmed.

papers.title: Regret bounds for sleeping experts and bandits (Kleinberg, Niculescu-Mizil, Sharma)
papers.claim: Near-optimal regret against the best-ordering benchmark for stochastic and adversarial rewards; a search snippet credits it with O~(sqrt(TK log T)) for stochastic rewards. Primary text not opened.

papers.title: Nearly Minimax-Optimal Regret for Linear Contextual Bandits with Arbitrary Adaptive Action Sets (Tianyuan Jin)
papers.claim: O~(K^{1/4} sqrt(dT)) for linear bandits with adaptive menus of size K, with a matching lower bound for K<=d and T>=d^2. Probably the source of the database's K^{3/4} sqrt(T) upper bound (d=K); the abstract does not address the K-armed special case.

triage.summary: I found no published result that removes the remaining log-factor gap in T (upper bound has a log^0.75 T factor, lower bound is a log-free √T). Jin (2026, arXiv:2609.15170) is the source of the database upper bound and covers adaptive action menus. Its abstract claims lower bounds that match up to logarithmic factors: Ω(K^{1/4}√(dT)) for K ≤ d and T ≥ d², and Ω(√(dT)·min{√d, (d log K / log 2d)^{1/4}}) for K ≥ d. These are much stronger than the database's σ√(dT)/(8√e) lower bound and seem to be missing from the database, but they still leave polylog factors. The 'open_known' label is soft: it rests on the paper's 'nearly minimax-optimal, up to logarithmic factors' wording, and no paper I saw explicitly calls the log factors an open problem. Caveats: I only read the abstract, not the theorems; the paper is an unreviewed single-author preprint; and the abstract never mentions i.i.d. contexts, so it is unconfirmed whether Jin's lower-bound construction applies if the key means truly i.i.d. stochastic contexts. Li, Wang, Zhou (arXiv:1904.00242) is listed for the small-K regime (n ≤ 2^{d/2}) only; I did not confirm that its construction fits this adaptive-menu key. Ruan, Yang, Zhou (arXiv:2007.01980) is listed for context only: it covers stochastic contexts but concerns how much adaptivity is needed, and does not tighten the regret log factors.

papers.title: Nearly Minimax-Optimal Regret for Linear Contextual Bandits with Arbitrary Adaptive Action Sets
papers.claim: Abstract claims (unreviewed preprint, abstract only read): upper bound Õ(K^{1/4}√(dT)) for 2 ≤ K ≤ d, with a matching lower bound Ω(K^{1/4}√(dT)) when T ≥ d²; for K ≥ d, upper bound Õ(√(dT)·min{√d, (d log K)^{1/4}}) and lower bound Ω(√(dT)·min{√d, (d log K / log 2d)^{1/4}}). Matching is only up to logarithmic factors, so the log gap in T remains.

papers.title: Nearly Minimax-Optimal Regret for Linearly Parameterized Bandits
papers.claim: Lower bound Ω(√(dT log T log n)) for n ≤ 2^{d/2} actions per round, matched by VCL SupLinUCB up to iterated-log factors. Covers the small-K regime only; not confirmed to fit the adaptive-menu key.

papers.title: Linear Bandits with Limited Adaptivity and Learning Distributional Optimal Design
papers.claim: With stochastic contexts, O(log log T) batches suffice for optimal regret. This concerns adaptivity and does not tighten the regret log factors.
